analysis.title: US Market Intel Morning Briefing, November 6, 2026
key_insights: Futures are up, led by Tech, as the market tries to bounce from its worst day since 'Liberation Day'. Semis and Memory are retracing about 30%-40% of the prior day's losses, and Mag7 and Software are also bid.
Nov 5 trading value was $1.74T, the highest since the June 26 rebalance. The JPM derivatives desk was very busy in VIX downside.

Today's question is whether the relief rally holds or selling and de-risking resume into the weekend. With recession fears tied to 'if AI fails or capex goes to zero', NFP may carry asymmetric downside risk: a beat is backward looking and a miss adds to fears.

European and Asian markets were down 1.2%-2.2% in Europe (UKX -2.0%, SX5E -1.5%, DAX -2.1%) and NKY -6.0%, KOSPI -6.0%. Moves were multiple standard deviations in many cases, and regional yield curves are flattening.

Ron Adler (Equity HT Cash Trading) says AI is the fulcrum of the market. Hyperscalers began funding ambitions via capital markets, and traders moved out the risk curve into picks-and-shovels names. Circular AI financing got too little scrutiny while things went well.

Adler cites stress signs: META raising money at 7.5%, a Chinese chipmaker putting its IPO on hold, MRVL down ~40% after the LITE deal announcement, and hedge fund stress. The midterm election may have tipped the scale by making datacenter growth harder in DC.

Crowding remains a pain point. HF long/short spreads are working today, JPM volumes are +50%, and client questions on pain levels, unwinding and fund stress are multiplying. Adler expects few to rush in to defend outside defensives.

Adler sees flows as directionally rational but the magnitude as surprising. He is constructive in one respect: a lot of positioning pain has been taken, and a harder path for datacenter expansion could ease pressure on capital markets and yields.

Feroli expects NFP of +75k vs the Street's +65k and a prior print of 29k, unemployment at 4.1% vs 4.2% prior, and average hourly earnings of +0.20% MoM and +2.8% YoY, a new cycle low. Options priced about a 0.9% move at the open, rising to about 1.6% by 1:30pm, on options expiring today.
Retail investors sold nearly $1.3bn by 12pm on Nov 5, a -6.2z event, concentrated in Mag7, Semis and levered ETFs.

Mark Schilsky (TMT) says SOXX was down 9% on Nov 5 with nowhere to hide: Megas down, Internet down regardless of AI exposure, and Software hit hard. He questions whether it was de-grossing, since popular shorts did not rally, and thinks Retail may have given up on the AI trade.

Brian Heavey (TMT) describes SOXX trading like a full stop-out, with hyperscalers reversing the prior day's gains. Retail selling was a -7.2z event, long-only funds were cutting semis and AI exposure, and SMH broke the 200-day with a possible test of April 1 levels.

Heavey says a harder political backdrop for datacenter buildouts is bad for what was the sole driver of US GDP growth. The AI datacenter trade depends on open capital markets, which appear to be closing quickly.

Brendan Henrici (Energy/Mats/Utils) says gold is a safe haven again, not just equity beta. Gold outperformed the S&P by 5%, the largest gap since February and the second largest in about 18 months, just as CTAs got short.

Henrici notes the JP1XVOLT grid/AI power basket traded 230m shares Nov 4 and was tracking 300m on Nov 5, over half a billion in two days, far above any two-day period in 3 years (DeepSeek peak was ~320m). It followed a 16% two-day drawdown, the largest since March 2020, which he calls capitulatory.

Briggs Barton (Consumer) sees a defensive shift: Retail index down ~300bps vs Staples up ~100bps, momentum down another 3%. Demand is tilted to quality leisure (VIK, LTH) and defensive/inflation plays (ORLY, AZO, TSCO), with large-cap staples flows (WMT, COST, KO, KDP).

JPM Market Intel stays Tactically Bullish. First, a prior-Friday style flush tends to rebound: when NDX is within ~6% of its high and falls 3.5%+, it rebounds ~3% the following week, more so if the drop was on a Friday.

Second, JPM argues this week's data can ease stagflation and recession fears: record household net worth, strong cash, checking balances up 5x since COVID, room to add debt, record corporate margins, and AI not a major hiring driver. CRWV employs only 550 people. The main effect would be lower capex and possible hyperscaler layoffs, plus a negative wealth effect if a bear market develops.

Third, the biggest non-AI risk is Middle East re-escalation. A WSJ report of damage to US regional bases by Iran and depleted munitions suggest another round could be limited and may push diplomacy. Oil appears to have priced this outcome, limiting upside for energy, yields and equity downside.
Lastly, seasonality turns positive: November is the strongest month on average this century, and post-midterm seasonality is a tailwind.

Monetization Menu (Nov 2): broadening can continue, with a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals weighted toward Cyclicals, a tactical Tech rebound, selectivity among AI winners and losers, and Consumers and Financials working if the curve steepens. Europe could catch a bid if US/Iran move to a deal. In Jan-Feb, US Value was +7.4%, SXXP +7.6% and UKX +9.7%.
Oct 26 menu suggested hedges via long oil/Energy equities and long vol. Oct 19 menu favored Tech rebound exposure via pairs and derivatives, Financials and Retailers, and Brazil and Japan.
Market snapshot: SPX +0.2%, NDX +1.2%, RTY -0.0%, WTI $90.63, NatGas $3.00, Gold $4,064, Silver $51.90, 10Y 4.849%, VIX 26.85.
Catalysts: NFP, unemployment and AHE at 8:30am ET Nov 6, UMich at 10am, NY Fed Williams at 4:30am. CPI Nov 10, PCE Nov 25, Retail Sales Nov 17, Fed meeting Dec 9, US funding deadline Dec 11.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM Market Intel stays Tactically Bullish: a 3.5%+ NDX decline near highs tends to rebound ~3% the next week, positioning pain has largely been taken, consumers and margins are strong, and November seasonality is positive.
tension_points.bear_case: Retail capitulation, closing capital markets for datacenter funding, circular financing worries, and crowding unwinds, with NFP carrying asymmetric downside risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak NFP print that adds to recession fears and further de-risking into the weekend.
